title: Flapping route: graceful shedding and pool-orchestration probe for partial-region dataplane loss
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: exercise end-to-end behavior when one region's dataplane GPUs intermittently become unreachable while the control plane and metadata remain available. We want to validate adaptive shedding, tenant fairness, routing fallbacks to other regions/model-variants, and that circuit-breaker cascades do not amplify into cross-region outage. The experiment focuses on: (1) flapping reachability to a subset of GPU hosts (simulate NIC-level packet loss and host-level transient OOMs), (2) inducing blocking dependency behavior (simulated datastore and auth blackholes) for callers routed via the affected region, and (3) verifying control-plane-driven mitigations (route reweighting, model variant fallback, admission-control triggers). The output should be a concise runbook, dashboards, and several post-run mitigations added to the product backlog.
acceptance_criteria: Run completes without customer-visible SLA violation >5% for non-affected tenants
Regional failover completes within 6s median and 20s 95th for new requests
No tenant experiences >2x baseline error rate for more than two consecutive minutes
Autoscaler does not overprovision >1.5x baseline capacity within 10 minutes of flapping start
Circuit-breaker tripping in region A must not cause >10% degradation in region B latencies
hypothesis: If we simulate short (30s–5m) intermittent dataplane losses on a region and concurrently blackhole a dependent metadata service for calls routed through that region, our routing and shedding controls (adaptive admission control, tenant-priority fairness, and model-variant fallback) should keep external SLOs within tolerances and avoid cross-region amplification by rapidly shifting traffic and throttling non-critical tenants.
repro_steps: Stage: deploy test workload that mimics RLHF-style distribution (mixture of short chat queries and long-batch generation) across region A and primary region B
Install chaos agent to selectively drop traffic to 40% of GPU hosts in region A in 30s windows with randomized jitter
Simultaneously configure dependency proxy to return TCP resets for a simulated datastore endpoint for callers with route=region-A for 60s windows
Enable debug routing logs and increase telemetry for KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, admission control metrics, and per-tenant error counts
Run for 3 hours with three flapping patterns: frequent short flaps (30s every 2m), moderate flaps (2m every 10m), and long flaps (5m every 30m)
tasks: Spec: finalize experiment parameters and acceptance criteria (owner: Maya)
Infra: provision chaos VMs and test GPU tenant pools (owner:Infra team)
Observability: create dashboard + alerting for SLO, per-route latency, model-variant fallback rate, admission-control rejections (owner: Observability)
Injector: implement dataplane dropout harness and dep-proxy blackhole toggles (owner: Reliability)
Run: execute staged runs (owner: Reliability + Oncall)
Postmortem: compile findings, mitigation proposals, and prioritized backlog items (owner: PM)
Follow-up: implement quick fixes (priority gating, improved fallback order) and schedule larger work (autoscaler tuning, route-weight smoothing)
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: Initial spec drafted after postmortem for incident-2026-02-07. Focus is on partial dataplane loss patterns we observed during the incident.
2026-02-20 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed infra requirements; requested that the injector can do both symmetric and asymmetric drops so we can test host-local vs rack-local blackouts.
2026-02-25 Infra: Chaos VMs provisioned in staging; GPU tenant pools cloned from prod-sim; note: need larger ephemeral quota for long-flap tests.
2026-03-02 Observability: Dashboard created; added query for per-tenant admission_reject_rate and model_fallback_count (see attachment).

2026-03-10 Reliability run 1: Ran short-flap pattern for 90 minutes. Observations: median failover ~5.4s, 95th ~18s; admission-control spiked for low-priority tenants causing >2x error rate for 3 minutes for two tenants — violates acceptance criterion. Root cause appears to be imbalance in tenant-weight calculation.
2026-03-11 Post-run: Decided immediate mitigation: cap admission-control rejection per-tenant and smooth route weights over 30s instead of instant reweighting. Filed quickfix ticket PM-4127.
2026-03-13 Liam O'Connor: Preparing second run after quickfix changes. Planning to include longer flaps and a higher ratio of long-batch jobs to stress KV cache eviction behavior.
